name: Strassen
kurzbeschreibung: Village in the Pustertal with a modern leisure pool and a nearby recreational area.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Strassen is situated at an elevation of 934 meters in the East Tyrolean Hochpustertal, spread across the sunny alluvial cone of the Thurnbach where it enters the Drau river. Home to approximately 800 residents in the district of Lienz, this tranquil village showcases authentic alpine farmsteads and living agricultural traditions. The dispersed community encompasses scenic hamlets such as Hof, Bach, Messensee, and Fronstadl, alongside the valley floor around Tassenbach. Framed by the rugged Lienz Dolomites, the Villgraten Mountains, and the Carnic Ridge, Strassen affords breathtaking panoramic views and marks the entrance into the pristine Tyrolean Gailtal.

Geschichte

The origins of Strassen are intrinsically tied to the ancient Roman road that once traversed the Pustertal toward the Roman city of Aguntum near Lienz, providing the village with its historic name. Strassen was first mentioned in official records in 1293 in connection with a hilltop chapel dedicated to St. Jakobus der Ältere. In 1453, Cardinal Nicholas of Cusa granted an indulgence to the sanctuary, prompting the construction of a late Gothic architectural jewel between 1455 and 1460. The parish church houses an extraordinary art treasure: late Gothic frescoes painted around 1458 by Master Leonhard von Brixen, depicting the Passion of Christ and the Works of Mercy, which were rediscovered and restored in 1936. In the hamlet of Hof stands the Church of the Holy Trinity (Filialkirche zur Heiligsten Dreifaltigkeit), an unusual late Baroque circular rotunda constructed between 1763 and 1768 by Thomas Mayr, embellished with ceiling frescoes by Franz Anton Zeiller.

Anreise

Reaching Strassen is straightforward by car and public transport. Drivers traveling from the north arrive via the Felbertauernstraße B108 to Lienz and continue westward on the Drautalstraße B100 directly to Strassen. From South Tyrol or Carinthia, travelers also use the B100, which connects at Tassenbach with the Gailtalstraße B111. The local railway station, Tassenbach, is located on the edge of the village and provides hourly train connections on the Pustertal railway line between Lienz and San Candido/Fortezza. Regional ÖBB buses link Strassen with Sillian, Lienz, and the Gailtal villages of Kartitsch and Obertilliach. Cycle travelers enjoy direct access to the Drauradweg R1.

Tipps

Art and culture enthusiasts should not miss a guided tour of the elevated parish church of St. Jakobus to marvel at Leonhard von Brixen's vibrant Gothic frescoes. For cyclists, the world-famous Drauradweg R1 provides an unforgettable family excursion: pedaling gently downhill along the Drau from Sillian past Strassen to Lienz, with bikes easily returned by train. A scenic drive along the Pustertaler Höhenstraße reveals historic mountain farmsteads and spectacular vantage points facing the Carnic Alps. During winter, visitors enjoy cross-country skiing along the snow-sure Grenzlandloipe as well as downhill skiing at nearby ski resorts Hochpustertal-Thurntaler and 3 Zinnen Dolomites.
